title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། པེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 182)
shelf_note: A Pramāṇa commentary folio from the Derge Tengyur (pe volume): it discusses qualifiers (ཁྱད་པར), the qualified entity (ཁྱད་པར་དང་ལྡན་པ) and the staff/staff-bearer example, which is standard tshad ma material.

tr_errors_A.english: we refer to them based on what is commonly known as the relationship of benefit
tr_errors_A.problem: Blurs the contrast with the next sentence: the Tibetan says that, in terms of what is accepted 'among us', the qualifier relation is rooted in benefited and benefactor, whereas for 'others' it is rooted in relation. A drops 'among us' and blurs the doctrinal contrast.

tr_errors_A.english: Therefore, in reality, if the entity is grasped as being related to all particulars
tr_errors_A.problem: དོན་ (the object) read as 'in reality'; the object becomes a vague 'the entity'.

tr_errors_A.english: If the related entities were distinct, they would not be understood…
tr_errors_A.problem: The page ends mid-sentence; A completes the fragment with a main clause that is not in the source.

tr_errors_A.english: it is not the case that everything is understood through a single entity. Even so,
tr_errors_A.problem: Breaks the 'even if … nevertheless' concession across a full stop, so the conditional reads as an assertion. The meaning can still be recovered.

tr_errors_B.problem: The Sanskrit equivalent is loose: the Tibetan means viśiṣṭa/viśeṣaṇavat (the qualified thing), not dharmin (property-bearer). The English gloss is right.
'Inherence' is a keyword that is not on the page; the text says only 'relation' (འབྲེལ་པ).

pages.prefer_reason: Neither has a serious error. B keeps the 'among us' vs 'others' doctrinal contrast and the 'even if … nevertheless' structure, and it leaves the final fragment open; A blurs the first, breaks the second and completes the fragment with a clause of its own.

book_verdict: A correct Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa leaf (marginal folio 353) with a clean transcription that matches the block print line by line. Both translations are usable; B is the more precise.
